newsitem.title: USA: US gasoline prices continue falling at pump - AAA.
newsitem.headline: US gasoline prices continue falling at pump - AAA.

text.p: Gasoline prices at the pump, continuing a trend in recent months, fell again this month tracking lower crude prices, according to a monthly survey published by the American Automobile Association (AAA).
Prices have also been pressured downward by the cushion of rising gasoline inventories, a AAA spokesman said.
"It's gone down a cent or two a month largely due to the higher inventories and the lower prices of crude oil," said AAA spokesman Bill Jackman.
The AAA said the average price of self-serve regular unleaded gasoline fell by 1.7 cents in the last month to $1.233 a gallon, or 4.1 cents below year-ago levels.
Light sweet crude oil futures prices closed on Tuesday at the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) at $19.67 a barrel, well below the close of $22.38 a barrel a year ago today.
On the inventory front, the American Petroleum Institute reported last week that gasoline inventories of 204.1 million barrels were 2.65 million over the prior year level.
Prices were lowest in the Southest at $1.15 a gallon -- down 2.0 cents in the last month and 3.9 cents lower than a year ago.
At the other extreme was the West Coast, where prices dipped just 0.3 cent and stood at a nationwide high of $1.352.

But that was 6.7 cents less than last year, just after California refiners had experienced a rash of serious outages that clipped supplies just at a time when crude and gasoline inventories were rebounding from 20-year lows.
Nationwide, prices this month are 5.5 cents lower than at the start of the year.
